recommended_title: How Accurate Is Regression-Based GATE Estimation Under Network Interference? Exposure-Mapping Fidelity Governs Error in an Eight-Case Grid
central_question: In a single randomized experiment on a network, how accurately can a regression-based estimator of the global average treatment effect (predict all-treated and all-control outcomes from exposure features, then difference) recover the truth, and which features of the interference mechanism, graph and assignment design determine when it works and when it fails?
central_thesis: On an eight-case synthetic grid (n=3000; SBM, Barabasi-Albert, Watts-Strogatz graphs; additive, strong, saturating, degree-dependent and two-hop interference; Bernoulli and cluster assignment), regression-based GATE error is small (about 3-5% relative RMSE per case) when the fitted exposure mapping matches the generating mechanism, is large and largely systematic when it does not (saturating and two-hop cases), and the nominal 95% intervals undercover (0.839 mean coverage), so accuracy is governed by exposure-mapping fidelity rather than by graph family, interference strength or assignment design within the tested range; a BIC-gated parametric exposure library lowers the sealed-final mean relative RMSE to 0.126 versus 0.180 for the plain linear exposure regression, but does not fix the two-hop case.
narrative_rationale: The sealed final evaluation is completed with outcome 'qualified' (final.qualification.outcome), 24 unseen seeds x 8 cases, no missing or failed episodes, and the four evaluator-owned baselines (difference-in-means, linear exposure regression, neighbourhood Horvitz-Thompson, correctly specified oracle regression) plus negative controls were run on the same instances. That supports a calibrated empirical paper on the research question posed in the task: how accurate, what determines the error, where it fails. The strongest grounded story is not 'a new estimator wins' but a thesis-first characterization: the per-case final errors (0.031-0.054 under additive/strong/cluster/graph-family variations, 0.151 degree-dependent count, 0.198 saturating, 0.452 two-hop) show that error tracks exposure-mapping misspecification, with the oracle (0.045) as the correct-specification reference and the linear baseline (0.180), DiM (0.622) and HT (0.994) as the cost of ignoring or non-parametrically using exposure. The frozen estimator is a vehicle to measure this, not the headline. The honest negative results (undercovering intervals, unresolved two-hop case, flexible ensemble and residual-correction variants failing to beat linear on the search plane) are retained as findings. Qualification is a measured-result statement only; it is not evidence of generality or validity beyond the eight declared cases.

method_groups.name: Frozen BIC-gated parametric exposure-regression GATE estimator (studied estimator)
method_groups.include_reason: It is the single frozen selection evaluated on the sealed final plane; library of OLS-fitted exposure mappings (linear neighbour fraction, treated-neighbour count, two-hop fraction, saturating/sigmoid shapes, degree and covariate interactions), analytic all-treated/all-control feature values, BIC-margin gate (margin 10) with linear fallback, HC1 delta-method interval widened by the departure from linear. Describe only what is in the program source; the gate's per-case behaviour is unknown (diagnostics unverified).

method_groups.name: Plain linear exposure regression (own treatment, neighbour-treated fraction, covariates)
method_groups.include_reason: Canonical regression-GATE estimator (Chin-style); final mean relative RMSE 0.180; the reference against which the frozen estimator's ratio 0.701 is reported.

method_groups.name: Difference-in-means and neighbourhood-exposure Horvitz-Thompson
method_groups.include_reason: Interference-ignorant and design-based comparators (final 0.622 and 0.994); show why modelling exposure matters and that HT is high-variance at n=3000.

method_groups.name: Oracle correctly specified exposure regression
method_groups.include_reason: Evaluator-owned reference (final 0.045) using the true mechanism form; marks the floor achievable by regression when specification is right, separating misspecification error from sampling error.

method_groups.name: Estimator-class alternatives on the search plane (flexible ridge ensemble with extrapolation-aware averaging; linear plus design-weighted residual correction)
method_groups.include_reason: Search-plane (8 seeds) scores 0.232 and 0.185 vs linear 0.184 show that added flexibility or residual correction did not help; presented as a clearly labelled search-plane comparison of estimator classes, never as final evidence and never as a chronology.

method_groups.name: Negative controls (constant outcome, permuted outcomes, permuted/relabelled graph) and deterministic replay
method_groups.include_reason: Validity checks on the frozen estimator: constant-outcome max |estimate| 9.0e-15, permuted-outcome mean relative estimate 0.0588, permuted-graph RMSE 0.627, 0 vacuity violations, replay difference 0, 0 missing/failed episodes.

results_focus: Headline accuracy view (final plane, 24 unseen seeds x 8 cases, n=3000): mean relative RMSE of the frozen estimator 0.126 vs oracle 0.045, linear 0.180, DiM 0.622, HT 0.994 (ratios 0.701 to linear, 0.203 to DiM). Relative error is min(|est-GATE|/|GATE|,2), RMSE per case then mean over cases; state this metric and why (scale-free across mechanisms with different GATE sizes, cap prevents HT blow-ups dominating).

Per-case error profile and single-factor contrasts (final.metric.rmse_rel_case_1..8): 1 SBM additive Bernoulli 0.051; 2 cluster design 0.031; 3 BA 0.054; 4 WS 0.040; 5 strong interference 0.034; 6 saturating sigmoid 0.198; 7 BA count x degree-dependent 0.151; 8 two-hop 0.452. Contrasts against case 1 (design, graph family, strength, response shape, spillover range) and case 3 vs 7 (mechanism form on BA). Within these cases graph family, interference strength and cluster vs Bernoulli assignment do not degrade accuracy; response-shape and spillover-range misspecification do. State that each contrast is a single case pair with 24 seeds and no per-case interval is available; hypothesis support is 'consistent with', not tested by factorial design.

Bias versus variance: mean absolute relative bias 0.074 against mean RMSE 0.126, i.e. a large systematic component aggregated over cases; per-case bias is not in the artifacts, so do not assign bias/variance split per case.

Uncertainty quantification of the intervals: coverage 0.839 against nominal 0.95 (mean over cases), mean relative width 0.379; report as undercoverage, a negative result. Per-case coverage is unavailable.

Seed-level variability: per-seed evaluator scores over the 24 final episodes (range about 0.078 to 0.180, two clear outliers at seeds 9001 and 9015); report mean, spread and a bootstrap interval computed from final.evidence.episodes, flagged as seed-level (plane-score) variability, not per-case.

Estimator-class comparison on the search plane only (8 seeds, same 8 case specifications, different seeds): flexible ridge ensemble 0.232, linear+residual correction 0.185, BIC-gated parametric library 0.140 vs linear 0.184 on that plane; per-case table shows that the gain concentrates in case 6 (0.708 to 0.267) while case 8 stays near 0.445. Selection of the frozen estimator happened on this plane; keep search and final separate and say final-plane numbers are the evidence.
Validity checks: negative controls and replay as above; interpret permuted-graph RMSE 0.627 (close to DiM level) as evidence that the estimator actually uses graph structure.
figure_plan: Fig. 1 (overview, early placement): conceptual schematic of regression-based GATE estimation: network + random assignment -> exposure features -> fitted outcome regression -> prediction at all-treated and all-control corners (rarely observed exposure states, extrapolation) -> GATE estimate; with the eight-case grid axes (graph family, response shape, spillover range, strength, assignment design) and the two error sources (sampling noise vs exposure-mapping misspecification).

Fig. 2 (main results, two panels): (a) aggregate mean relative RMSE for oracle / frozen estimator / linear / DiM / HT on the final plane (log or broken axis because HT and DiM dwarf the others); (b) per-case relative RMSE of the frozen estimator on the final plane ordered by the factor varied from case 1, annotated with the oracle aggregate and linear aggregate as reference lines.

Fig. 3 (reliability, two panels): (a) strip/dot plot of the 24 per-seed final scores with mean and bootstrap interval; (b) interval coverage 0.839 against the nominal 0.95 line with relative width annotated.
Table 1: factor-contrast table mapping each of the 8 cases to graph, response form, strength, design, with final per-case relative RMSE.
Table 2: search-plane estimator-class comparison (3 variants x 8 cases + mean + bias + coverage) with linear baseline reference, labelled as search plane.

notes_for_writer: Final evaluation is completed with outcome 'qualified' (final.qualification.outcome, status completed, correct true). Say so plainly, but treat qualification as a statement about the measured result on the declared eight-case grid, not as evidence of generality, validity beyond the grid, or superiority of the gated estimator. There is no downstream_study block; make no downstream claims.

Keep search and final separate. Search plane: 8 seeds (101-108), 3 scored model variants, all scored (no unscored attempts). Final plane: 24 unseen seeds (9001-9024). The search and final planes use the same eight case specifications with different seeds, and the BIC-gated library was designed after seeing search-plane per-case errors (cases 6 and 8 were the identified headroom). Therefore the final gain over linear shows seed-level out-of-sample behaviour on known mechanism families, not transfer to new mechanisms. State this as a limitation in the main text.

Numbers must come from final.metric.* and final.evidence.episodes (final) or result.improvement_00x / search per-case metrics (search). Round consistently (three decimals). Use the term 'relative RMSE' with the definition min(|est-GATE|/|GATE|, 2) aggregated as RMSE per case then unweighted mean over 8 cases; do not use pipeline names.

Per-case baseline numbers (DiM, linear, HT, oracle) are NOT available; only plane-level aggregates. Do not claim per-case comparisons to linear or oracle, and do not claim which cases drive the linear baseline's 0.180. The oracle is a reference to correct specification only in aggregate.

Bias/variance: only the aggregate mean absolute relative bias (0.074) is available on the final plane. Do not claim per-case bias-dominance for cases 6 and 8 on the final plane; the search-plane bias figure (0.092 for the selected variant vs RMSE 0.140) may be cited as search-plane only.

The persistent two-hop failure (case 8: 0.452 final, 0.445 search) has an unknown cause: the library contained a two-hop-fraction mapping, but gate diagnostics are unverified and absent. Report that the cause is unresolved, offer hypotheses (gate not firing, two-hop fraction mapping misspecified relative to the generating walk-normalized feature, corner extrapolation) explicitly as hypotheses, and do not assert a mechanism.

Do not distinguish statistical failures from validity or adaptivity failures except where evidence identifies the cause; the interval undercoverage (0.839 vs 0.95) is an observed outcome, its cause is not established.

Gaps to disclose in limitations: one graph size (n=3000), one assignment probability (0.5), single-factor contrasts via case pairs not a factorial design, no per-case uncertainty intervals, synthetic mechanisms known to a family level, no real or public-graph (Facebook100/SNAP) experiments in the artifacts, no ablation of the BIC gate margin or library components (ablation_studies is empty), no GNN or learned graph-covariate methods. State that these were not done rather than implying they were.

Related work to cite from references.bib only for entries relevant to the topic: regression adjustment for global effects (Chin), randomization-based interference (Aronow and Samii), cluster randomization and network experiments (Ugander randomized graph cluster randomization, Karrer network experimentation at scale), model-based regression adjustment with model-free covariates (Han and Ugander), optimized covariance design (Chen et al.), low-order outcomes and clustered designs (Eichhorn et al.), plus other interference estimators present in the bib (Forastiere et al., Offer-Westort et al., Shankar et al., Lu et al.) where they genuinely fit. Ignore irrelevant bib entries (medical meta-regression, climate, nephrology etc.). Verify each reference's content from references_provenance.json before citing; do not cite starter-list papers that are not in references.bib (e.g. Eckles et al., Cortez et al., Kipf and Welling, Defferrard et al.) unless added with provenance.

Novelty claim must be modest: the contribution is a quantified, scoped characterization of regression-GATE accuracy and failure modes with a transparent evaluation protocol, controls, and an honest negative result on interval calibration, not a new theory. Do not claim a bound or theorem; none is in the artifacts.

Venue (ICLR 2026): double-blind, no self-identifying links or paths, 8 to 9 body pages with the final page at least 75 percent full, a separate LLM Usage section (may be in the appendix), single-column template. Spend body space on: problem framing and notation (about 1 page, including Fig. 1), related work (0.75), setup, estimator and metric (1.5), results with Fig. 2, Table 1, Fig. 3, Table 2 (3 to 3.5), discussion and limitations (1). No padding.

Figure implementation: matplotlib quantitative figures exported to both PDF and PNG (300 DPI) from the same source script; reference the PDF in LaTeX. Raster-only fallback must be at least 2400 px wide for full-width placement. Only one figure (overview_schematic) uses generate-concept-figure. Fig. 2 panel a needs a log or broken axis since HT (0.994) and DiM (0.622) dwarf the others; label values directly. Use one consistent color per method across all figures and keep fonts at 8pt or larger at final size. Per-seed values for Fig. 3a come from final.evidence.episodes; bootstrap CI is computed from those 24 values and described as seed-level.
Thresholded rates: none are planned. If one is added, define a reader-facing meaning such as fraction of seeds with relative error below a stated level, and use one threshold per figure.

Use reader-facing terms: 'model variant' for candidate estimators, 'configuration' for implementations, 'seeded run' for runs. Describe the three search-plane variants as estimator classes compared on a held-out-seed search plane, in thesis order, not discovery order.
